instruction: I'm learning Vim and want to improve code readability. Search online for how to enable syntax highlighting in Vim permanently and configure my local Vim to use syntax highlighting by default.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)

metadata.explanation: Task requires searching online for Vim syntax highlighting configuration, then editing ~/.vimrc to add 'syntax on' or 'syntax enable'. The evaluator checks if the .vimrc file contains the proper syntax enabling command.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies that .vimrc contains 'syntax on' or 'syntax enable' which enables syntax highlighting by default
Script uses correct regex pattern '^[[:space:]]*(syntax on|syntax enable)' which properly handles leading whitespace (spaces/tabs)
Getter executes shell script via vm_command_line which correctly extracts configuration state from .vimrc file
Metric check_include_exclude correctly verifies success message in output
Complete coverage: instruction requires configuring Vim for syntax highlighting by default, evaluator verifies the configuration exists
Minor edge case: script doesn't distinguish commented vs uncommented lines (e.g., '# syntax on' would match), but this is unlikely in practice
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding negative lookbehind to exclude commented lines: grep -E -q '^[[:space:]]*[^#]*(syntax on|syntax enable)' to avoid matching '# syntax on'
